title: Add a bulb side by side: what changes?
hook: A second bulb joins the first, side by side. Do they share, or does the battery pay more?

knows: current flows round a loop and makes bulbs glow
volts, amps and ohms as words on a battery or bulb
the same current flows all round a single loop
doesNotKnow: that each parallel branch gets the full battery voltage
that branch currents add at a junction

misconception: Adding a second bulb in parallel splits a fixed current between them, so each glows dimmer and the battery gives the same total.
objective: The learner can explain that each parallel branch has the full battery voltage across it and draws its own current, so the battery supplies the sum: two 6 ohm bulbs on 6 V draw 1.0 A each and 2.0 A in total.

claims.text: Bulbs in parallel each have the full battery voltage across them, and the branch currents add up to the current the battery supplies.
claims.source: Kirchhoff's voltage and current laws. Halliday, Resnick and Walker, Fundamentals of Physics, ch. 27 (resistors in parallel).

claims.text: A 6 ohm bulb on 6 V draws 1.0 A; with two in parallel the battery supplies 2.0 A, and with three 3.0 A.
claims.source: I = V / R = 6 / 6 = 1.0 A per branch; totals 1 + 1 = 2.0 A and 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.0 A.

claims.text: Two 6 ohm bulbs in parallel act like a single 3 ohm resistor.
claims.source: 1 / (1/6 + 1/6) = 3 ohm; 6 V / 3 ohm = 2.0 A, matching the sum of branch currents.

claims.text: Each parallel bulb glows just as brightly as the bulb did alone.
claims.source: Power per bulb P = V^2 / R = 36 / 6 = 6 W, independent of how many branches there are (ideal battery).

claims.text: The lesson assumes an ideal battery and bulbs of fixed 6 ohm resistance; real bulb filaments have higher resistance when hot, and real batteries sag under more current.
claims.source: Stated on the stage ('Ideal battery. Each bulb 6 ohm.') and in the reveal. Tungsten resistance rises roughly tenfold from cold to operating temperature (Halliday, Resnick and Walker, ch. 26, temperature coefficient of resistivity).

recall.question: You plug a second identical lamp into another socket of the same wall circuit. The current drawn from the supply…
options: stays the same, shared between the lamps
recall.why: Sockets are in parallel: each lamp gets the full voltage and draws its own current, and the supply provides the sum.
